author: v. j. decker
title: Franklin County Public Utilities announces lawn irrigation schedule due to drought conditions
text:
Franklin County Public Utilities announced on April 29 that a new lawn irrigation schedule is now in effect as a result of ongoing drought conditions.
The measure aims to help manage limited water resources during the drought period. Residents are required to follow specific watering schedules based on their street address number, with odd-numbered addresses allowed to irrigate lawns on Tuesdays and Saturdays, and even-numbered addresses on Wednesdays and Sundays. For automatic or non-automatic irrigation systems, watering is permitted from midnight until 10:00 a.m. Hose-end sprinklers and hand-held hoses may be used between 6:00 a.m. and 10:00 a.m., as well as from 6:00 p.m. to 10:00 p.m., following the same odd/even day pattern.
Vehicle washing currently has no restrictions but must use an auto shut-off nozzle. Pressure washing is only allowed on Saturdays and Sundays, while no outdoor watering of any kind is permitted on Mondays, Thursdays, or Fridays.
“Franklin County is working hard to manage our available resources and your cooperation in this effort will be greatly appreciated,” the department said in its announcement.
In related community data, recent figures show that college readiness remains an area of focus for local schools. Of senior students taking the science portion of the ACT in Franklin County school districts during the 2022-23 school year, about 14.9 percent were considered ready for college according to the North Carolina Department of Public Instruction. Among juniors taking the same test, approximately 13.1 percent met college readiness benchmarks according to the department.
For reading proficiency, around 23.9 percent of seniors demonstrated college readiness based on ACT results reported by the North Carolina Department of Public Instruction, while among juniors it was about 22.5 percent according to the department. In math, data shows that about 12.7 percent of seniors were considered ready for college according to the North Carolina Department of Public Instruction, with juniors at roughly 10.9 percent according to the department.
Residents with questions regarding the new water use schedule are encouraged by officials to contact Franklin County Public Utilities at (919)556-6177 or visit www.FCPU.us.
